sources.citation: Pick, Andrew N. 2020. A Reconstruction of Proto-Northern Adelbert Phonology and Lexicon. PhD dissertation, University of Hawai'i at Manoa.
sources.note: Glottolog lists it as a subclassification reference for Kare, but the text never mentions Kare; its stress discussion covers Northern Adelbert languages (Mauwake, Pamosu, Usan) only.

sources.citation: Z'graggen, J. A. 1971. Classificatory and typological studies in languages of the Madang District. Pacific Linguistics C-19. Canberra: ANU.
sources.note: Same stress-omitted remark on p. 6; 'Typological Features of the Mabuso Stock' (p. 35) lists segmental features only (Kare: prenasalised voiced stops, no glottal stop, no /h/); the 'none of the languages appears to be tonal' lines apply to the Adelbert Range Phylum (p. 73) and Ramu stocks, not Mabuso/Kare.

'KARE: 340 (1969 Z'Graggen). Madang Province.. Mabuso group'; 12th ed. '..Mabuso, Kare. Survey needed.' — confirming no SIL survey then.

sources.citation: Pawley, Andrew & Harald Hammarström. 2018. The Trans New Guinea family. In Bill Palmer (ed.), The Languages and Linguistics of the New Guinea Area: A Comprehensive Guide, 21-195. Berlin: De Gruyter Mouton.
sources.note: Appears only in the annotated classification list (speaker figure + best available source, here a wordlist), confirming no phonology exists; the prosody overview (sec. 2.4, 'In languages of the Madang and Finisterre-Huon groups.. tone and pitch accent are largely absent') is group-level and names no target language.
sources.venue: The Languages and Linguistics of the New Guinea Area: A Comprehensive Guide

sources.citation: Pawley, Andrew. 2001. The Proto Trans New Guinea obstruents: arguments from top-down reconstruction. In A. Pawley, M. Ross & D. Tryon (eds), The Boy from Bundaberg: Studies in Melanesian linguistics in honour of Tom Dutton, 261-300. Pacific Linguistics 514. Canberra: ANU.
sources.note: Nothing: Kare appears only as lexical forms without stress marks in cognate sets; the paper is about obstruent correspondences. Text searched for stress/tone/tonal: no Kare-related hit. Listed for completeness as an open work that uses Kare data; PDF read in the work dir and deleted (not kept: no phonology of Kare).

sources.citation: Roberts, John R. 1997. Switch-reference in Papua New Guinea: a preliminary survey. In Andrew Pawley (ed.), Papers in Papuan Linguistics No. 3, 101-241. Pacific Linguistics A-87. Canberra: ANU.
sources.note: No phonology content. Its value is negative evidence from an SIL-PNG insider with access to unpublished SIL materials in 1997: sec. 2.2.54 'For a miscellaneous number of Papuan language families in Madang Province we have no information as to whether the languages of these families have SSIDS or not. These are: Yaganon, Peka, Kare, Dimir..'; appendix table: 'Kare family ?SR Madang Z'graggen (1975)'. I.e. no grammatical or phonological description of Kare existed in SIL or published sources as of 1997.

sources.citation: Z'graggen, J. A. 1980. A comparative word list of the Mabuso languages, Madang Province, Papua New Guinea. Pacific Linguistics D-32. Canberra: ANU.
sources.note: Introduction (pp. v-ix) and transcription note (p. viii, semi-phonemic transcription; Kare lacks voiced/voiceless fluctuation and the labio-velar stop) say nothing about stress; no stress marks in the Kare (C1) column.
